chunks: "It was named Minā because Ibrāhīm عليه السلام wished there that Allah would place, in place of his son, a ram that He would command him to slaughter as a ransom for him."

key_terms.إِبْرَاهِيمَ: Ibrāhīm عليه السلام, the Prophet connected to the sacrificial trial
key_terms.فِدْيَةً: as a ransom or redeeming substitute
key_terms.كَبْشًا: a ram offered in place of the son
key_terms.مِنًى: Minā, the sacred site associated with the rites of hajj

ai.seo_question: Why was Minā given this name in relation to Ibrāhīm عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This narration explains the naming of Minā by linking it to the wish of Ibrāhīm عليه السلام during the trial of sacrifice. It reflects the sacred memory of devotion, ransom, and divine testing associated with the rites of hajj.
